# Definition
A ***symmetric matrix*** is a matrix $A$ such that $A^\top = A$, and a ***skew-symmetric matrix*** is a matrix $A$ such that $A^\top = -A$.

# Theorem
**(i)** $A + A^\top$ is symmetric for any square matrix $A$.

**(ii)** $A - A^\top$ is skew-symmetric for any square matrix $A$.

**(iii)** Every square matrix can be uniquely expressed by a sum of a symmetric matrix and skew-symmetric matrix. In particular, for any square matrix $A$,

$$A = \frac{A+A^\top}{2} + \frac{A-A^\top}{2}$$

# Reference
- S. H. Friedberg, A. J. Insel, and L. E. Spence, Linear Algebra, 4th ed. (Pearson New International Edition), Pearson, 2013.
- 곽진호, 핵심선형대수학, 개정 3판, 경문사, 2023.
